prompt: If $0.25x + 1.5 = 0.4x - 0.6$, what is the value of $x$?
hint: The decimals make this look harder than it is. The steps are the same as for whole numbers, or you can scale every term to clear them.

hints.text: The decimals make this look harder than it is. The steps are the same as for whole numbers, or you can scale every term to clear them.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try it with friendlier numbers first: $0.5x = 2$. Multiply both sides by $10$ to get $5x = 20$, so $x = 4$. Scaling away the decimals works the same way no matter how many terms there are.
Multiply every term by $100$ to get $25x + 150 = 40x - 60$, then collect the $x$ terms on the right and the numbers on the left.
Subtracting $25x$ and adding $60$ gives $210 = 15x$, so the answer is $x = 14$.

learningObjective: Solve a linear equation with decimal coefficients.
explanation: Multiply every term by $100$ to remove the decimals, which keeps the equation balanced: $25x + 150 = 40x - 60$.
Subtract $25x$ from both sides so that $x$ appears only on the right: $150 = 15x - 60$.
Add $60$ to both sides to collect the constants: $210 = 15x$.
Divide by $15$ to get $x = 14$. A check gives $0.25(14) + 1.5 = 5$ and $0.4(14) - 0.6 = 5$, so the value of $x$ is $14$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Clear decimals with Desmos, or by hand
steps: Faster still: graph $y_1 = 0.25x + 1.5$ and $y_2 = 0.4x - 0.6$ in Desmos and click the intersection.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Treat the −0.6 as +0.6 and you get 0.9 = 0.15x, so x = 6 — a clean-looking wrong answer built from one dropped sign.
Move both constants across in a single written step and then verify x = 14 in the original equation; the check costs ten seconds and catches exactly this slip.
